restatements.text: Requires individuals keeping a firearm in a residence to store it in a locked container when not carried or used.
Directs the Department to issue a storage certificate to applicants for a $25 fee.
Preempts all city and county ordinances regarding firearm storage, establishing that the act occupies the entire field of regulation.

analysis.answer: Current law has no state rules on residential firearm storage, allowing cities and counties to adopt their own ordinances. The measure establishes a statewide mandate to store unattended firearms in a locked container, introduces a $25 storage certificate, and strips local governments of the power to regulate firearm storage.

Direct costs include the $25 fee for the storage certificate and the purchase price of a locked container for those who do not already own one. Opportunity costs include the time spent completing the certificate application process.

Firearm owners bear the costs of the fee and the required storage containers. The state Department receives the fee revenue. Firearm owners benefit from a uniform statewide standard instead of varying local rules, while residents may benefit from potentially reduced unauthorized access to firearms.

Many firearm owners will likely purchase lockboxes or safes to comply, though some may ignore the mandate given the difficulty of enforcement inside private homes. The Department will need to establish a system to process applications and issue certificates. Local governments with existing storage ordinances will have to stop enforcing them.

The measure addresses the risk of unauthorized access to firearms and the complexity of varying local storage laws. The locked-container requirement directly targets unauthorized access, though it relies heavily on voluntary compliance. The preemption clause effectively resolves the patchwork of local rules by centralizing authority at the state level.
The state legislature and the Department gain power over firearm storage policy and administration. Cities and counties lose their regulatory authority over the issue.

The effectiveness of safe storage laws in reducing accidental shootings and suicides is broadly supported by public health research, though researchers sometimes debate the exact magnitude of the effect and the level of actual compliance among firearm owners.
A portion of the $25 fee revenue will be absorbed by the Department's administrative costs to process applications, verify payments, and issue the certificates.
As a statutory measure, it can be amended or repealed by the legislature through the normal legislative process.

flags.note: The text requires a "locked container" without defining what types of devices (e.g., safes, lockboxes, trigger locks) meet this standard.

flags.quote: The Department shall issue a storage certificate to each applicant
